n: In March 1829 Martin Harris, still wanting proof after losing the 116 pages, asked for a witness that Joseph truly had the plates. The Lord answers through Joseph.

f.w: Martin Harris
f.g: a prosperous Palmyra farmer who financed the printing of the Book of Mormon and became one of the Three Witnesses.

n: Joseph is to tell Martin that the Lord gave him the plates and commanded him to be a witness of them.

f.w: stand as a witness of these things

n: Joseph had covenanted to show the plates only to those the Lord designated, and he had no power over them except what God granted.

f.w: you should not show them except to those persons to whom I commanded you

n: Translating was Joseph’s first gift, and he was to focus on it alone, claiming no other gift until the translation was finished.

f.w: pretend to no other gift
f.g: “pretend” here means to claim or lay claim to, not to fake.

n: Sorrow will come to the world if people refuse to listen to the Lord’s words.
Joseph will later be ordained and sent to deliver God’s word. This came true when he received the priesthood a few months later.

f.w: hereafter you shall be ordained

n: If people won’t believe God’s word, they wouldn’t believe Joseph even if he could show them the plates. Physical evidence doesn’t create faith.

f.w: if they will not believe my words, they would not believe you

n: The Lord expresses displeasure with an unbelieving, stubborn generation.

f.w: stiffnecked
f.g: stubborn and proud, like an ox that refuses to bend its neck to the yoke.

n: The plates themselves are being kept back for a wise purpose and will be made known to future generations.

f.w: for a wise purpose

n: This generation will receive God’s word through Joseph’s translation rather than through seeing the plates.
Three other servants will be called to see the plates and testify along with Joseph. These became the Three Witnesses: Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and Martin Harris.

f.w: the testimony of three of my servants

n: Their certainty will come from heaven itself — God will declare the truth to them.

f.w: from heaven will I declare it unto them

n: God will give these witnesses the power to see the plates as they really are.

No one else in this generation will receive this same witness as the church emerges “out of the wilderness.” The poetic phrases describe the church’s beauty and strength, drawn from the Song of Solomon.

f.w: clear as the moon, and fair as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners
out of the wilderness

n: God repeats that he will send forth his word with the testimony of three witnesses.

f.w: the testimony of three witnesses

n: Everyone who believes God’s words will receive the Spirit’s witness and be born again through baptism of water and of the Spirit. Personal revelation is available to all, not just the witnesses.

f.w: born of me, even of water and of the Spirit

n: A brief aside: Joseph must wait a little longer, because he has not yet been ordained.

f.w: ye are not yet ordained

n: The witnesses’ testimony will also stand as condemnation against those who harden their hearts.
A “desolating scourge” — widespread calamity — will repeatedly afflict the earth if people do not repent, until the wicked are consumed at Christ’s coming.

f.w: a desolating scourge
the brightness of my coming

n: Just as the Lord warned the people of Jerusalem of their destruction and it came true, these warnings will also be fulfilled.

f.w: the destruction of Jerusalem

n: The Lord commands Joseph to repent, live more uprightly, and stop yielding to other people’s pressure — a clear reference to the lost manuscript episode.

f.w: yield to the persuasions of men no more

n: If Joseph stays firm in keeping the commandments, he is promised eternal life — even if he should be killed. This promise foreshadows his martyrdom in 1844.

f.w: even if you should be slain

n: The Lord returns to Martin Harris, the man asking for a witness.
Martin is too proud and has not humbled himself enough. But if he will bow down in sincere, mighty prayer, he will see what he desires — which happened in June 1829.

f.w: humble himself in mighty prayer

n: Then Martin can testify that he saw the things shown to Joseph by God’s power, not man’s.

f.w: by the power of God and not of man
f.g: The Testimony of Three Witnesses in the Book of Mormon uses similar language.

n: Martin’s testimony should be simple and limited: he has seen them by God’s power. Nothing more.
If Martin denies this testimony, he will break his covenant and be condemned.
Unless Martin humbles himself, admits his wrongs, covenants to keep the commandments, and exercises faith, he will not receive this vision.
If Martin will not humble himself, Joseph should tell him to stop pressing the Lord on this matter.
In that case, Joseph is to translate a few more pages and then pause until the Lord commands him to resume.

f.w: thou shalt stop for a season

n: If Joseph disobeys, he will lose his gift and the sacred things entrusted to him.

f.w: thou shalt have no more gift

n: The Lord foresees enemies plotting against Joseph, and warns that Martin will fall into transgression if he doesn’t humble himself and receive the witness.

f.w: lying in wait to destroy thee

n: Many seek Joseph’s life. These commandments are given to protect him and prolong his days.
“Stop, and stand still” — the Lord will provide a way for Joseph to accomplish the work. God’s timing and means will be sufficient.

f.w: stand still

n: If Joseph remains faithful, he will be lifted up at the last day — exalted in God’s presence.

f.w: lifted up at the last day
